title: 4521-ESP-ANC-00-62-0002 Specification for Insulation Subcontract

summary_points: Contract allows alternate billing cycles other than thirty days.
Owner can pay within 180 days after certification and approval.
Information is confidential and proprietary to Abener.
Initialing required on cover sheet; all title block info on all pages.
Revisions are noted in the body of the Specification.
Purpose: Define work scope, insulating materials, and guidelines for solar plant insulation.
Contractor responsible for all requirements except agreed-upon exceptions.
Imperative language directed to Insulation Subcontractor unless otherwise specified.
Contract allows alternate billing cycles, extended payment and certification periods.
Information is confidential and proprietary.
Insulation must cover all equipment, vessels, tanks, and piping.
Contractor responsible for labor, materials, and supervision.
Vendor responsible for slight variations in installations.
Contract allows alternate billing cycles, extended payment, and certification/approval periods.
Materials must be new, commercially available, and free of defects.
Insulation installation after painting, inspection, heat tracing, and pressure testing.
Vessels, equipment, piping, and ductwork must be 100% insulated.
Confidential information must not be disclosed without permission.
Owner can request payment within 180 days after certification and approval of billings and estimates.
Insulation must be applied to a height of 7 feet above grade and 2 feet from walkways/platforms.
All insulating work must be performed in a neat, high-quality manner.
Wet or damp insulation must be replaced with dry insulation.
Insulation and jacketing must allow for thermal expansion without creating gaps or hot spots.
Insulation and jacketing must be protected from mechanical damage during construction.
Finished edges of jacketing surfaces should have a neat, clean appearance.
Equipment nameplates and code inspection plates must not be covered.
Pre-formed or molded pipe insulation segments for vessels up to 42” in diameter are acceptable.
Payment within 180 days after certification and approval is allowed.
Insulation must be applied in standard length sections, preferably 36" when possible.
All insulation should have staggered joint construction with at least 2” overlap.
Manway and access way covers should be insulated separately.
Flanges and valves should be insulated unless otherwise specified.
Insulation on flanges and valves must be removable without damaging adjacent insulation.
Insulation on valve bodies should not interfere with adjustment or removal of the packing gland.
Insulation must match adjacent pipe material and thickness, extend to specific components, and be secured properly.
Stainless steel wire/bands used for securing insulation, with spacing requirements.
Non-code items include specific methods for applying insulation over stiffeners, surfaces, and painted stainless steel.
ASME coded items have restrictions on field welding and require specific strapping bands for cylindrical surfaces.
Payment within 180 days after certification and approval of billings is allowed.
Certification and approval within 30 days after receipt of billings is allowed.
